As Microsoft's new OS is coming to life as each week passes, I started to ask friends and coworkers their opinions on Windows 10. Due to the fact that I only asked about two people so far that actually care, I can't help but feel that my survey pool is biased and restrictive. Accordingly, I've come here to ask an audience with a broader range of opinions of technology their opinion.

What is your opinion on Microsoft's upcoming operating system, Windows 10, in its current state?
Q: What is your opinion on Windows 10 as it stands?
I haven't gotten it yet, but I heard that it's free to those with Windows 8.1. Would you recommend getting it, if you have it?

I haven't tried Windows 10; only seen the official announcments, demos, commercials, etc. Man, even just seeing them, the OS has definitely caught my interest. Yeah, you're right, except that it will also be a free upgrade for Windows 7 SP1 users as well (both upgrades are valid within a year).

Anyway, the reason it caught my interest is because it looks a lot like classic Windows in how it handles things. Instead of apps being full screen and controls optimized for touch, the Windows 10 team listened to the complaints and made what I call "the second Windows 7", with window-able Windows apps, a hybrid of the start screen and start menu, more multitasking functionality natively built-in, and I hear it should perform better than Windows 8.1. I'm not sure about anyone else here, but, when Windows 8 came out, I thought I was going to be one of those XP users who didn't want to switch because of the direction Microsoft was taking. But, with Windows 10, especially their integrity with admitting their mistakes by offering it for free, will definitely be the upgrade I make.

I just hope my essential programs will work in addition to a custom font-smoother like MacType, since I'm not a fan of Microsoft's cleartype.

I haven't seen it yet, but I have very high hopes for it. I really think that it's likely going to be to Winders 8 what Winders 7 was to Visturd. It's kinda sad, because Winders 8 was pretty awesome under the hood. The real issues were that the product mangler wanted to 'make his mark' and refused to listen to focus groups or anyone else who didn't agree with his vision. Winders 8 could have been killer. Winders 10 looks to fix all of that nasty unfriendly UI nonsense.

Can't say I've heard much about it. I have heard, correct me if I'm wrong, that they've made it so that metro isn't shoved quite as far down your throat as it was in Windows 8. That makes it better right away in my opinion. Metro is pretty but generally just seems to make it harder to get to the actual information and settings you find yourself needing.

I am, however, starting to very seriously consider switching to any of the Linux distros, perhaps even entirely. The main thing keeping me back is vidya, but I will certainly be installing it in my non-gaming computers when I get the chance. By the time I get used to it, it may be the case that Windows 10 may be completely irrelevant to me as I've gone full Linux.

Interesting. I'm a fan of the open source movement, so I've considered switching to Linux before, but I'm not sure the option for me to do so would be available to me anytime soon. There's just too much software that I need on a daily basis, like a good video editor, my video games, and a few other specific software. Otherwise, I would have already switched.

I can certainly understand where you're coming from, there certainly is a lot of software that just won't work on Linux. For me, there's not really much that isn't already supported or there's a good enough or equivalent that exists already.I may have even already done it when I formatted and did a fresh install of my computer a month or two ago, but at that point I didn't want to go through the process of reformatting all my drives again and making sure my data is safe. Next time I'll consider it is when I get whatever modest gaming rig I come up with and get that together. I'll probably at least try one of the kinder distros like Mint and start to get used to it, if anything just to make myself get used to it.

Thinking about it though, I'll probably always have at least two windows machines for the near future. I'd like to have a windows machine just because I find myself having to do tech support/data recovery for people sometimes, and having a windows machine usually that makes it easier. Then I'll still have an old computer running XP for similar reasons. So I doubt I'll ever be full Richard Stallman-kin for that reason.

I haven't used the beta, only seen screenshots, but it sounds like that Microsoft has realized that they made a mistake with Windows 8. Windows 8 wasn't designed to work well for the desktop - it fails to recognise the differences between tablets and desktops. As long as those mistakes are fixed, I expect everyone will naturally follow the upgrade cycle to Windows 10, especially given the free updates.

I've used the windows 10 tech/home insider preview for a few months now as my main OS to get a feel for it. Here is a list of things that I like/dislike about it:

Pros

  • near borderless windows, makes everything much less cluttered. It doesn't seem like much at first, but if you start using Windows Vista/7/8 it starts bothering you right away.

  • Cortana integration. While I haven't found myself using this a lot, the two commands that I appreciate the most are the calculator and the dictionary. The ease of access this provides makes the small little things just that bit easier. Of course if you don't have cortana listening for you ("Hey Cortana, ...") it's easier just to pull up a calculator program or a new browser tab and do it the old way.

  • The ability to have windows phone apps as normal windows. This is huge for me. As an example, I only use Facebook for its messaging, so I have the Windows Phone app running on my desktop, with only the messenger displayed, fixing a lot of the aesthetic design and loading problems of Facebook.

  • The start menu can now be pulled up on whatever screen is most convenient for you.

Neither really bad or good

  • The new, flat aesthetic. It looks nice and clean, but I'm not sure how I like it overall. It can grate on you a bit. For those who don't know what I'm talking about

Cons

  • Multi-monitor glitchiness. A lot of strange buggy things happen when you try and run games and such on fullscreen on a multi-monitor setup. The biggest and most common problem I encountered was that the windows key would be emulated as pressed whenever a game went fullscreen, and if I clicked a part pf the full screen program that would be blocked it would tab out of the window, bringing me to the next problem. I fixed this by making sure to have the start menu opened before the game launched.

  • Alt-Tab glitchiness. As a general rule, if I alt-tabbed out of a full screen application, it would not alt-tab back in.

  • No volume ding. The last time I checked, when you adjusted the volume, it did not make the ding noise that tests volume noise. However, if you go into volume mixer, it will make a new ding noise, which means it will probably be implemented fully in the final release.

tl;dr: It's better than windows vista or 8, but I wouldn't recommend an upgrade until alt-tabbing works completely.

(Note I am on vacation, and as such, the last time I used an up to date tech preview was 6/7)

Insightful! I haven't tried the preview because their terms kind of pushed me away, so it's nice to hear from someone who's been on the inside.

All three of those cons are pretty relevant in my home workspace, so I hope they get fixed before release. All in all, I hope Windows 10 does the multi-monitor a lot better than its predecessors. Otherwise, I always have my DisplayFusion.

I find the flat design direction Microsoft's heading in better than their aero glass with glowy controls asthetic they had with Vista and 7, but still not something I'm fond of, which is why I have been using third-party full themes ever since I first got 7. I might try the new look for a little while and decide whether or not I'll do the same for 10.

Having owned a Windows Phone for two years, I am happy to see both Cortana integration and the fact that WP apps work on desktop in their own window. I believe that this could be what Microsoft needs to grab more attention for their Windows Store.

I really appreciate the comment!
